newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sammi Steel plant resumes operations.
newsitem.headline: Sammi Steel plant resumes operations.

text.p: South Korea's troubled Sammi Steel Co said on Wednesday it has resumed operations of its stainless steel plate plant in southeastern industrial city of Changwon.
The 200,000 tonnes-a-year plant was shut down shortly after Sammi defaulted on its debt repayments in March, a company spokesman said. It has another plant in Ulsan, near Changwon.
The spokesman said the company's employees had collected about four billion won and bought 2,000 tonnes of hot coils, the feed stock for the plant.
He did not give further details.
"We have enough feed to last for about a month," he said. "Looking at our self-rescue efforts, we hope suppliers of the feed stock will offer new supplies on credit."
Sammi Steel's financial troubles has earlier led to the sales of part of its specialty iron rod production business in February to Pohang Iron and Steel Co.
Sammi sought court protection on March 19 and defaulted on debt repayments a day later.
